transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
A New York federal judge is ordering the Justice Department
to reinstate former prosecutor Maureen Comey,
who was fired last year, the latest from NPR's Nate Perez.
The ruling calls for Maureen Comey to receive back pay,
dating to when she was fired last year,
and for her to return as a prosecutor
to the Southern District of New York if she chooses.
Judge Jesse Furman wrote in the opinion
that the Department of Justice invented
a new and expansive theory of executive power
and violated her constitutional right to due process.
The department never gave a performance-based reason
for her dismissal.
In a lawsuit last month,
Maureen Comey alleged that the real reason she was fired
was because her father is James Comey,
the former FBI director who drew President Trump's ire.
In an emailed statement, the Justice Department
said it would appeal the decision.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
With just over a week to go before Election Day,
Democrats know that to win control of the Senate,
they have to gain ground in unexpected places.
NPR's Sage Miller reports one of those places
is in rural Ohio, where the Senate contest
is unusually competitive.
Ohio has been a reliably red state in the last few elections,
and so are rural voters for the most part.
President Trump won rural America by 40 points in 2024,
but recent polling shows his approval rating
is rocky there, too.
Matthew White is a longtime resident
of the small Appalachian town of Athens, Ohio.
-There's a lot of people in rural Ohio that are not happy,
whether it's gas prices, diesel prices, the tariffs, the war.
-Democrats are trying to gain ground in rural Ohio
to get the Senate majority back.
Both Senate candidates have been investing heavily
in rural Ohio because they know
it just might be the ticket to victory.
Sage Miller, NPR News.
-Iranian officials insist they remain open to diplomacy
but stand ready for war.
More from NPR's Hideo Al-Shalchi.
-The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson
said that his country is ready to continue talks with the US,
but that it was also preparing itself for "any scenario."
Alex Vatanka of the Middle East Institute
says the Iranian regime is built to resist.
-This is a regime that will fight,
and it would look to the outside world
as an unnecessary, costly, crazy fight,
but that's the nature of the regime.
-He says Iran thinks at some point
President Trump will have to cut his losses.
While Trump has claimed in the past
that Iran's military infrastructure has been destroyed,
Iran was able to retaliate forcefully
in a second round of strikes in June.
Analysts say that with the help of China and Russia,
Iran could continue to replenish its military arsenal.
Hideo Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
-Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekhov in "Star Trek,"
the original series, and a number of movies
that followed, died yesterday.
Representatives say the cause was old age.
He was 90 years old.
It's "NPR News."
Eric Bowser, the modern voice behind some of Looney Tunes'
most beloved characters, has died,
according to a statement on his Instagram page.
His family writes the Emmy-award-winning actor
passed away suddenly.
They did not disclose a cause of death,
but write that more details are to come.
In an interview earlier this year with host Jonathan Buckley
on the Warner Brothers TV podcast,
Bowser invokes some of the characters
that he says he watched and analyzed
over years of "couch potato-ing."
-So we got Bugs Bunny. -That's right.
-Daffy Duck. -Yeah, yeah.
-Pokey Pig. -Yeah, sometimes.
-Marvin the Martian.
-Yes, isn't that lovely?
-Eric Bowser was 46 years old.
Students are still missing more school
than before the pandemic.
Chronic absenteeism occurs when students
miss more than 10% of the school year,
and Piazza Nakimeta has the latest.
-We'll start with the good news.
More students have been coming to school
regularly in the last few years,
but attendance still isn't where it was before the pandemic.
It's all in a new report from five organizations
that focus on chronic absenteeism,
and the reasons for absences have changed.
For example, families are more cautious
about sickness since COVID.
Recent immigration crackdowns have led some parents
to keep their kids at home,
and students also report feeling less connected
when they're at school.
Building strong relationships with students,
making class more engaging,
and making sure there's reliable transportation
are among some of the strategies schools can use
to keep improving attendance.
-Janakimeta, NPR News. I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
-Wanna hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now,
sponsor free through Amazon Music,
or you can also support NPR's vital journalism
and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Federal judge orders DOJ to reinstate fired prosecutor Maureen Comey with back pay
Rural Ohio emerges as key battleground in competitive Senate race ahead of Election Day
Iran says it remains open to diplomacy with US while preparing for any scenario
Walter Koenig, original Star Trek actor who played Chekhov, dies at 90
Eric Bowser, voice of Looney Tunes characters, dies suddenly at age 46
Chronic absenteeism remains above pre-pandemic levels, new report finds, with changing reasons for absences
